assessment.nobel_worthiness: A genuine new window on the universe: discovery of a diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos at TeV-PeV energies with a cubic-kilometre detector, then identification of first sources (TXS 0506+056 in 2017-18, NGC 1068 in 2022) and the Galactic plane in 2023. This is exactly a discovery found by clues from nature, with clear lasting impact for multimessenger astronomy and cosmic-ray origin.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led IceCube and pushed the Antarctic-ice concept; Karle was a central figure in building and operating the detector. Yoshida is credited but I regard his role as less decisive. The collaboration is large, so a prize to two or three people necessarily simplifies credit; the AMANDA precursor and the DUMAND lineage complicate the picture (my recollection, not verified here).
assessment.maturity: Strong and independent confirmation of the diffuse flux, multiple source associations at several sigma, and a consistent interpretation. Timely; the discovery is now more than a decade old and the field is established.
uncertainties: Source-identification evidence (NGC 1068, TXS) is at a few sigma and the population origin of most events remains open.
Fair allocation among IceCube leadership, AMANDA pioneers and other founders is not settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Prediction of flat bands at the magic angle in twisted bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity opened the entire field of twistronics and moire materials. Original, clear, and demonstrably fertile across many labs.
assessment.attribution: The Bistritzer-MacDonald theory identified the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group delivered the decisive 2018 experiments. This is a natural theory-plus-experiment trio with a clean story, though other contributors (for example Cao, Fatemi, Dean, Yankowitz and Kim groups) played significant roles.
assessment.maturity: Many independent reproductions and a broad body of follow-up work. Interpretation of the superconducting mechanism is still debated, but the discovery itself is solid. Timely.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism of superconductivity is unresolved.
Credit among first-author experimentalists and parallel groups may be contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and realised to 10^-18 fractional uncertainty, have transformed time-keeping and now enable tests of fundamental constants, relativistic redshift at the millimetre scale and prospective redefinition of the second. Clear and original, with large impact.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed and first demonstrated the magic-wavelength lattice concept; Ye's group drove the strontium clock to the highest accuracy and demonstrated many-body clock physics. Two laureates is a clean configuration; Hall and Hansch were already honoured in 2005 for the comb technology.
assessment.maturity: Several independent labs worldwide reach consistent performance and clock comparisons confirm the results. Mature and timely.
uncertainties: Overlap in recognition with the 2005 prize for the frequency comb and with ion-clock work (Wineland 2012).
Other pioneers such as Lemonde, Derevianko or Pal'chikov are not in the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The BeppoSAX discovery of X-ray afterglows (1997) followed by optical afterglows and redshift measurements settled the long-standing question of the origin of gamma-ray bursts as cosmological events, opening a route to the most distant explosions and to the GRB-supernova connection. Decisive observational discovery.
assessment.attribution: Costa and Frontera led the BeppoSAX team that localised and detected afterglows; Kulkarni's group provided the pivotal optical/radio follow-up and redshifts. Other candidates for credit (van Paradijs, Djorgovski, Metzger, Piro, Heise) are not in the credited names, so the allocation is a defensible but contested simplification.
assessment.maturity: Fully confirmed for over two decades by Swift and Fermi and by gravitational-wave counterparts; a mature interpretation, arguably somewhat late.
uncertainties: Who deserves credit among the BeppoSAX, optical and radio follow-up teams is disputed.
Possible concern about the prize's fit with earlier cosmology and astrophysics awards.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics created the architecture used by most superconducting quantum processors, enabling strong coupling of artificial atoms to microwave photons and quantum non-demolition readout. Highly original and consequential, and recent recognition of superconducting circuits (2025 prize) makes the theme topical.
assessment.attribution: The Blais-Huang-Wallraff-Girvin-Schoelkopf 2004 proposal and Wallraff et al. 2004 experiment define the origin; Schoelkopf's group developed it into transmon-era technology. I choose Schoelkopf, Wallraff and Blais; Girvin's theoretical role is substantial and I am not confident of the best three.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced across many laboratories and platforms; technological use is wide. The question is whether it is a distinct enough discovery from the macroscopic-quantum-tunnelling work already recognised.
uncertainties: Allocation among four credited names is awkward; Girvin or Devoret-linked early work may be viewed as more fundamental.
Closeness to the recently awarded 2025 topic.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background from pulsar timing arrays (2023) opens the nanohertz gravitational-wave band and bears on supermassive black-hole binaries and possibly new physics. Exciting and a clear clue from nature.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread across the NANOGrav, EPTA, PPTA, InPTA and CPTA collaborations; Manchester, Kramer and McLaughlin are plausible representatives of the long pulsar-timing effort, but the decisive individual contributions are not obvious from the supplied names. This is a major attribution problem.
assessment.maturity: Premature for a prize: evidence is around 3-4 sigma, the Hellings-Downs correlation is not yet unambiguous at discovery level, and the astrophysical source (binaries versus cosmological) is unresolved.
uncertainties: Detection significance has not reached the conventional 5 sigma.
Source interpretation and allocation across four or five collaborations are unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Baryon acoustic oscillations as a standard ruler give one of the cleanest geometric probes of expansion history and dark energy, tied to the physics of the early plasma. Very relevant to cosmology and my own interest in dark energy, and clearly confirmed in galaxy surveys.
assessment.attribution: Eisenstein et al. (SDSS) and Cole et al. (2dFGRS) made the 2005 detections; Sunyaev and Zeldovich (with Peebles and Yu) predicted the acoustic features in the early 1970s. Zeldovich is deceased and Peebles and Yu are not in the credited list, so the proposed trio gives an incomplete and awkward history.
assessment.maturity: Many independent surveys confirm BAO and the measurement is mature. Recent DESI hints of evolving dark energy show continued importance, but it is more a tool than a stand-alone discovery.
uncertainties: Whether this is a discovery or a measurement technique is debatable.
Credit omits Peebles, Yu and others.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum simulation of Hubbard physics with ultracold atoms in optical lattices (superfluid-Mott transition, single-site imaging, antiferromagnetic correlations) offers a controllable laboratory for many-body physics. It is conceptually important and widely adopted.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch, Cirac) proposed the Bose-Hubbard realisation; Bloch and Greiner carried out the experiments and microscopy. The 2002 Mott-insulator experiment is central. Cirac is also credited; with a limit of three I choose Bloch, Greiner and Zoller, and the choice is uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Well established, reproduced widely, though the promised solution of open problems such as high-Tc Hubbard physics is still ongoing.
uncertainties: Overlaps with the 2012 prize for quantum control of atoms and 2001 BEC prize.
Choice among Cirac, Zoller, Jaksch and the experimental pioneers (Esslinger, Greiner, Bloch) is uncertain.
